name: Syria
region: Nationwide — Northwest, Northeast, Damascus, Deir ez-Zor
summary: Syria is in a complex transitional period following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024. While over 3 million displaced people have returned, conditions remain fragile with ongoing clashes in the northeast, the worst drought in 36 years, and 16.5 million people still in need of humanitarian assistance.
context:
The fall of the Assad regime in December 2024 marked a dramatic turning point in Syria's 13-year civil war, but it did not end the humanitarian crisis. Over 3 million displaced Syrians have returned home since December 2024, representing one of the largest return movements in years. However, the conditions they are returning to are deeply challenging: 77% of communities report a lack of livelihoods, and much of Syria's infrastructure — schools, hospitals, water systems — remains destroyed.

Ongoing clashes continue in northeastern Syria between Turkish-backed forces, Kurdish-led groups, and remnants of various armed factions. Explosive ordnance left by 13 years of conflict killed over 540 people in 2025 alone. The political transition is fragile, with competing armed groups and governance structures creating uncertainty across the country.

Syria is also experiencing its worst drought in 36 years, devastating agricultural production and water supplies in a country where millions already live in extreme poverty. 7.1 million people face food insecurity. The healthcare system, already decimated by the war, is struggling to meet the surge in need from returning populations.

Approximately 5.5–6 million Syrians remain internally displaced, and 3.9 million are refugees abroad — primarily in Turkey, Lebanon, and Jordan. The $3.19 billion humanitarian appeal for 2026 was only 36% funded, severely limiting the international community's ability to support Syria's transition.

Syria's reconstruction will require decades and hundreds of billions of dollars. The transition represents an opportunity, but without sustained international engagement and funding, the country risks sliding back into conflict or entrenching new forms of instability.

donate.name: UNHCR — Syria
donate.description: Supporting displaced Syrians returning home and those still in displacement with shelter, legal aid, and essential services.

donate.name: WFP — Syria Emergency
donate.description: Providing food assistance and livelihood support to millions of Syrians, including those returning to communities devastated by 13 years of war.

donate.name: WHO — Syria
donate.description: Rebuilding health systems and delivering medicines and vaccines across Syria, where hundreds of hospitals were destroyed or damaged during the war.

donate.name: ICRC — Syria
donate.description: Providing emergency healthcare, tracing missing persons, and supporting communities affected by the ongoing presence of explosive ordnance.

awareness: Share that 16.5 million Syrians still need humanitarian assistance despite the end of the Assad regime — the crisis did not end with the political transition
Highlight that explosive ordnance from 13 years of war continues killing civilians daily — demining is urgent and chronically underfunded
Amplify Syrian civil society voices working to shape the transition toward a just, inclusive, and rights-respecting governance
Raise awareness about the 3.9 million Syrian refugees still unable to safely return — political transition does not automatically create safe conditions
Challenge the narrative that Syria is 'fixed' — the 36-year worst drought, lack of livelihoods, and unstable security mean reconstruction is just beginning
political: Urge your government to substantially increase contributions to the 2026 Syria humanitarian appeal — currently only 36% funded
Advocate for the lifting of sanctions that impede humanitarian relief and reconstruction, while maintaining targeted measures against war criminals
Push for sustained international investment in Syria's transition process, including support for accountable governance and civil society
Demand that Syrian refugees in Turkey, Lebanon, and Jordan be protected from forced return to areas that are not yet safe
Support international accountability mechanisms investigating Assad-era atrocities, including enforced disappearances and chemical weapon use
